clue.text: Energy-filled paintings found around 505 AD

indicators.note: Energy-filled paintings means the word for paintings has the energy letter put into it
found around says the paintings word also goes round the Roman numerals, ahead of the energy letter

parts.note: paintings collectively are art
in Roman numerals 500 is D and 5 is V
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Art historians date some energetic paintings to around the year 505 AD.
explanation.walkthrough: AD looks like part of a date, but it is the definition, the short form of the answer; 505 is read as Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: An ad is the short form of advertisement, which is exactly what an advert is too.

clue.text: Places lots might go in suits around university

indicators.note: the word for suits is placed around the university letter

parts.note: lawsuits are legal actions

explanation.surface: Someone wonders where a large number of things might end up, dressed in suits near a university.
explanation.definitionFit: At a sale by bidding, items are offered in numbered lots, so auctions are where lots go.

clue.text: Very quick to go topless, being tasteless

indicators.note: going topless means losing the top, so the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: quick means rapid

explanation.surface: Someone who hurriedly strips off their top is judged to be lacking in taste.
explanation.definitionFit: Vapid means dull and insipid, offering nothing stimulating, the same as bland or tasteless.

clue.text: Dick about in Bible study? That's not easy!

parts.note: RI is Religious Instruction, the old school name for Bible study
C, for circa, means about
something not easy is hard

explanation.surface: A student called Dick finds his religious studies class a real struggle.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes Dick a man in a Bible class; it is the definition, since Dick is a pet form of the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Dick is a traditional familiar form of the given name Richard, as in Dick Whittington.

clue.text: Hoskins is normal, Independent admitted … my boss? Defective!

parts.note: the setter is Hoskins, so Hoskins is becomes I'M

indicators.note: Independent admitted means the letter I is let into the word for normal

parts.note: par is the normal standard, as in golf
a crossword setter's boss is the editor, ED

explanation.surface: The setter rambles about being normal at the Independent newspaper, before turning on the editor as defective.
explanation.definitionFit: Impaired means damaged or weakened in function, so something impaired is faulty or defective.

clue.text: Butch physicist who worked on speed and bit of oxy

parts.note: Ernst Mach studied supersonic speed; Mach numbers are named after him

indicators.note: a bit of oxy is just its opening letter

explanation.surface: A tough-looking scientist who studied speed seems to sniff a little oxygen.
explanation.definitionFit: Macho describes aggressively masculine behaviour, the same sense as butch for a manly, tough person.

clue.text: Let off bangers primarily with a crack outside

indicators.note: the a-plus-crack pair goes on the outside of the single letter

parts.note: to crack a problem is to solve it

indicators.note: primarily means take only the first letter of bangers

explanation.surface: Fireworks being let off, with a crack, as bangers explode on Bonfire Night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let off' looks like setting off bangers (firecrackers) but means pardon.
explanation.definitionFit: To absolve someone is to free them from blame or guilt, which is letting them off.

clue.text: Pressure to charge at gunner ordering offensive

indicators.note: to charge something is to load it, so the pressure letter is loaded into the rearranged letters
ordering the letters means putting at gunner into a new arrangement

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: An artillery officer is being pressured into ordering a charge in an offensive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offensive' looks like a military attack, matching the gunner, but it is an adjective meaning distasteful.
explanation.definitionFit: Repugnant means causing strong disgust or distaste, the same as offensive in the sense of objectionable.

clue.text: Some aficionado rating a Hungarian music producer

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A fan rates a recording made by a musician from Hungary.
explanation.definitionFit: Antal Dorati was a Hungarian-born conductor, who produces music by directing an orchestra.

clue.text: Policeman seen with Shaft can be a venomous beast

parts.note: Sting was the lead singer of the band The Police, so a Policeman
a shaft of light is a ray

explanation.surface: A police officer accompanied by the private eye Shaft is a dangerous creature.
explanation.walkthrough: Policeman is not an officer but a member of the band The Police; Shaft is not the film detective but a beam of light.
explanation.definitionFit: A stingray is a flat fish with a barbed tail that can deliver poison.

clue.text: Excellent American officer gets jerk snorting whizz

indicators.note: snorting means taking in through the nose, so the whizz word is drawn inside the officer-plus-jerk pair

parts.note: cop is an American word for a police officer
a tic is an involuntary jerk of a muscle
a whizz is an expert, an ace; whizz is also slang for amphetamine

explanation.surface: A US policeman finds some idiot snorting speed (whizz is British slang for amphetamine).
explanation.definitionFit: Copacetic is American slang for fine, satisfactory or very good.

clue.text: Drink beer to get half out of it? Wicked!

parts.note: to sup is to drink

indicators.text: to get half out of it
indicators.note: half of the word beer is to be got out, leaving its back half

explanation.surface: Someone drinks beer to get half-drunk, which they think is wicked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wicked' looks like a moral judgement but is slang approval, like great.
explanation.definitionFit: As slang exclamations both mean excellent or fantastic, used to express enthusiasm.

clue.text: I help vacuous neo-Nazi to change ways

indicators.note: changing direction of travel means the letters are read the other way

parts.note: to help is to aid

indicators.note: vacuous means empty, so only the outer letters of neo-Nazi remain

explanation.surface: The speaker claims to be helping a brainless neo-Nazi mend his ways.
explanation.walkthrough: I looks like the speaker but is the definition, the letter's codeword.
explanation.definitionFit: In the NATO phonetic alphabet used by radio operators, the letter I is spoken as India.

clue.text: One full of gas going red when turned on by hooker

definitions.text: One full of gas going red when turned on by hooker

parts.words: One full of gas going red when turned on by hooker
parts.note: a tube of the noble gas glows red when switched on, and a red lamp is the classic sign of a prostitute's premises

explanation.walkthrough: 'turned on by hooker' suggests arousal, but it means switched on by a prostitute, whose window shows a red lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: This glowing sign is a tube containing an inert gas that gives off a red-orange glow when electricity passes through.

clue.text: Earned bucks (around grand) with fewer clothes on!

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the grand letter
a horse that bucks throws things about, so the letters of earned are tossed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging
K, for a thousand, is slang for a grand

explanation.surface: A stripper made a lot of money, about a thousand, by wearing less.
explanation.definitionFit: Nakeder is the comparative of naked: more undressed, wearing less.

clue.text: Charles is one man to catch rare crustacean

parts.note: Charles III is a king

indicators.note: catching means holding, so the man word holds the rare letter

parts.note: a pawn is a chess man

explanation.surface: King Charles is a man trying to catch a rare shellfish.
explanation.definitionFit: A king prawn is a large prawn, a shellfish of the decapod order.

clue.text: Little piggy possibly seen with kid and swine

parts.note: in the nursery rhyme This Little Piggy, each piggy is a toe
to kid is to tease or rag

explanation.surface: A piglet is seen alongside a young goat and a pig.
explanation.walkthrough: Toerag is British slang for a contemptible person.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are insults for a nasty, despicable person, a rotter.

clue.text: English politician in trials creates uproars

indicators.note: the English politician goes in the trials word

parts.note: trials are tests
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An English MP on trial causes a huge fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: A tempest is a violent storm, and figuratively a tumult or commotion, an uproar.

clue.text: Bloody people can be despicable individuals

definitions.meaning: first meaning: people who are bleeding, or haemophiliacs
second meaning: British slang for contemptible people, rotters

explanation.walkthrough: Bloody looks like a swear word, but read literally it is people covered in blood.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally, people who lose blood; as British slang, a bleeder is a rotten or wretched person.

clue.text: Where a painter might do white lines to some extent

definitions.text: Where a painter might do white lines
definitions.meaning: first meaning: ..., as in a road, where white road markings are painted
second meaning: the phrase for partly, in some respects

explanation.walkthrough: Doing white lines suggests cocaine, but here it is a road painter marking lanes in a way, a road.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means partly or in some respects, a hedge expressing a limited degree.

clue.text: The Royal Family's flatulence painful? Take drug!

parts.note: flatulence is wind

indicators.note: take means remove, so the drug letter is taken from the painful word

parts.note: painful means sore
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: The royals suffer agonising gas and are advised to take medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: Windsor has been the surname of the British royal house since 1917.

clue.text: Union-based strike rejected by Congress and a Liberal

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the strike word is read in reverse

parts.note: to ram is to strike
IT is slang for sex, and congress here means sexual intercourse

explanation.surface: A trade-union strike has been voted down by Congress and a Liberal politician.
explanation.walkthrough: Union looks like a trade union and Congress the US legislature; both turn on marriage and sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Marital means relating to marriage, which is a union of a couple.

clue.text: Weary, on being taken by revolutionary in the sack?

indicators.note: being taken by means held inside, so the weary word goes into the revolutionary word

parts.note: a red is a communist revolutionary
to weary is to tire

explanation.surface: A tired communist goes off to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the sack' suggests being fired, but here it is bed: retired means gone to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To retire is to go to bed for the night, and the sack is slang for bed.

clue.text: Dope more expensive, society found in studies

indicators.note: the society letter is found inside the other pair

parts.note: dope and gen are both slang for information
prices that are up are higher

explanation.surface: Studies find that drugs have become dearer.
explanation.walkthrough: Dope looks like drugs, but it means inside information, as does gen.
explanation.definitionFit: To gen up is British slang for to learn about something, so gens up means studies.

clue.text: Dear old Hoskins has put on pound by end of binges

indicators.note: in an across answer, put on means placed after the other pieces

parts.note: ex means former or old
a pound is an enclosure, a pen

indicators.note: the end of binges is its last letter

parts.note: the setter Hoskins says I have, written I'VE

explanation.surface: The former setter Hoskins has put on a pound after his binges.
explanation.definitionFit: Dear means costing a lot of money, which is what expensive means.

clue.text: What might stem a leaky hooter? Timeless problem!

indicators.note: time-less means without the letter T, the abbreviation for time, so it is removed

parts.words: What might stem a leaky hooter
parts.note: a tissue stops a runny nose; hooter is slang for nose

explanation.surface: Someone with a runny nose has no time to find a hanky.
explanation.definitionFit: An issue is a matter for debate or concern, a problem.

clue.text: Zapata? A revolutionary led by original bit of thinking!

indicators.note: led by means the first-letter piece goes in front
the original bit of thinking is its first letter

parts.note: Che Guevara was a revolutionary

explanation.surface: Emiliano Zapata, the Mexican revolutionary, is credited with an original idea.
explanation.walkthrough: Zapata seems to be the revolutionary, but a Zapata is a drooping moustache style named after him; the question mark marks the example.
explanation.definitionFit: A tache is informal British for a moustache, and the Zapata is one style.

clue.text: Commanding Officer has trapped wind in foreign capital

indicators.note: trapped means held inside, so the officer letters go around the wind word

parts.note: a wind is moving air

explanation.surface: An army commander suffers from trapped wind on a trip abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Cairo is the capital city of Egypt, a capital abroad for the British reader.

clue.text: What yours truly does to save a couple of bums?

definitions.text: What yours truly does to save a couple of bums?

parts.words: What yours truly does to save a couple of bums?
parts.note: the setter keeps places for two people, and bums is slang for backsides, which are themselves sat on what is wanted

explanation.walkthrough: Bums suggests layabouts or backsides; the answer is both the places for backsides and what one does to keep them for others.
explanation.definitionFit: Places to sit, kept for two people, are chairs reserved for a couple of backsides.

clue.text: Dismal piece from Nyman? Took the piss about that!

parts.note: to have sat an exam is to have taken it

indicators.note: took the piss goes about the single letter, placed between its parts

parts.note: piss is urine

indicators.note: a piece from Nyman is just its first letter

explanation.surface: A critic mocked a gloomy composition by Michael Nyman, the British composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturnine means gloomy and morose in temperament, linked with the planet Saturn.

clue.text: Places one might see some sauce or hand in knickers

definitions.text: Places one might see some sauce

indicators.note: the hand letter goes in the knickers word

parts.note: knickers are panties
R stands for right, as in right hand

explanation.surface: A cheeky picture of someone with their hand inside their underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: Sauce suggests cheekiness, but it is literal: bottles of sauce are kept in larders.
explanation.definitionFit: Pantries are small storerooms for food, where condiments might be kept.

clue.text: Offensive old actor's admission repelled American

indicators.note: repelled means driven back, so these letters are read in reverse

parts.note: a performer admits I do, as in I act
US is the United States, American

explanation.surface: An aging actor's confession has disgusted an American.
explanation.definitionFit: Odious means hateful and repugnant, which is offensive in the sense of objectionable.
